title: Dasharatha arrives at Mithila
introduction: Dasharatha arrives at Mithila and Janaka receives him reverentially, as he belongs to a crowning dynasty, called Ikshvaku-s. Then, after the usual exchange of royal pleasantries and protocol, all of them stay in Mithila comfortably.
closing: इति वाल्मीकिरामायणे आदिकाव्ये बालकाण्डे एकोनसप्ततितमः सर्गः
Thus, this is the 69th chapter in Bala Kanda of Valmiki Ramayana, the First Epic poem of India.

verses.devanagari:
ततो रात्र्यां व्यतीतायां सोपाध्यायः सबान्धवः |
राजा दशरथो हृष्टः सुमंत्रमिदमब्रवीत्
verses.iast:
tato rātryām vyatītāyām sa upādhyāyaḥ sa bāndhavaḥ |
rājā daśaratho hṛṣṭaḥ sumantram idam abravīt
verses.translation: On the next dawn that heartened king Dasharatha who is with his teachers and his relatives then said this to his minister Sumantra.

glosses.meaning: then, night, on being elapsed [into next dawn]

verses.devanagari:
अद्य सर्वे धनाध्यक्षा धनमादाय पुष्कलम् |
व्रजंत्वग्रे सुविहिता नानारत्नसमन्विताः
verses.iast:
adya sarve dhana adhyakṣā dhanam ādāya puṣkalam |
vrajanti agre su vihitā nānā ratna samanvitāḥ
verses.translation: "Now let the chancellors of exchequers draw ample riches, gems and numerous other items that are used in the marriage from bridegroom's side, all-inclusively, and let them travel in advance and let them be well-prepared for any exigency...

glosses.meaning: numerous, gems [where gems are, upa lakshaNa, the subjunctive items among the items that are used in marriages from bridegroom's side,] all-inclusive

verses.devanagari:
चतुरंगबलं चापि शीघ्रं निर्यातु सर्वशः |
ममाज्ञा समकालं च यानं युग्ममनुत्तमम्
verses.iast:
caturaṅga balam ca api śīghram niryātu sarvaśaḥ |
mama ājñā samakālam ca yānam yugmam anuttamam
verses.translation: "Let the quadruple forces start off in a trice from everywhere at my order, and others shall start with unexcelled vehicles like palanquins, sedan chairs, litters etc., and with those that can be yoked with horses, like cabined-coaches and horse-carriages...
notes: The fourfold army is generally taken as horses, elephants, chariots, and foot soldiers for the word caturanga balam , while some say such an army is moved only when a massive combat is necessary, but not when going to marriages. Thus some say though army is moved, it is as much as required. But this word also qualifies as caturanga balam= dhana, kanaka, vastu, vaahana sampatti, the quadruple opulence, namely 'riches, gold, equipage, and vehicles...' where opulence will be the only show in Indian marriages, either of poor or rich. R. C. Dutt comes near to this when telling in his poetic version: 'Ride in front with royal riches, gold and gems in bright array /

glosses.meaning: even with, time, also [in a trice at my order]
vehicles palanquins, sedan chairs, litters etc]
that can be yoked [cabined-coaches with horses]

verses.devanagari:
वसिष्ठो वामदेवश्च जाबालिरथ काश्यपः |
मार्कण्डेयश्च दीर्घायुर्ऋषिः कात्यायनस्तथा
एते द्विजाः प्रयान्त्वग्रे स्यंदनं योजयस्व मे |
यथा कालात्ययो न स्याद्दूता हि त्वरयन्ति माम्
verses.iast:
vasiṣṭho vāmadevaḥ ca jābāliḥ atha kāśyapaḥ |
mārkaṇḍeyaḥ ca dīrghāyuḥ ṛṣiḥ kātyāyanaḥ tathā
ete dvijāḥ prayāntu agre syandanam yojayasva me |
yathā kāla atyayo na syāt dūtā hi tvarayanti mām
verses.translation: "Vashishta, Vaamadeva, Jaabaali and Kaashyapa, and the long-lived Maarkandeya, and Sage Kaatyaayana... let these Brahmans travel in forefront... and let horses be yoked to my royal-cariole, and as the messengers of Janaka are hastening me arrange for the travel without time lapse..." Thus Dasharatha ordered.

glosses.meaning: long, lived one - one who has longevity, Maarkandeya, also
my, royal-cariole, let it be yoked [with horses]
time, lapse, as to how, will not, will be there

verses.devanagari:
वचनाच्च नरेन्द्रस्य सेना च चतुरंगिणी |
राजानमृषिभिः सार्धं व्रजंतं पृष्ठतोऽन्वगात्
verses.iast:
vacanāt ca narendrasya senā ca caturaṅgiṇī |
rājānam ṛṣibhiḥ sārdham vrajantam pṛṣṭhato anvagāt
verses.translation: On the word of that best king the fourfold opulence, and even the fourfold forces up to some extent followed rearward of the king who is going after the sages who are going afore of him.

glosses.meaning: the best king's, by the word of

verses.devanagari:
गत्वा चतुरहं मार्गं विदेहानभ्युपेयिवान् |
राजा तु जनकः श्रीमान् श्रुत्वा पूजामकल्पयत्
verses.iast:
gatvā catur aham mārgam videhān abhyupeyivān |
rājā tu janakaḥ śrīmān śrutvā pūjām akalpayat
verses.translation: Travelling on a four-day-route Dasharatha reached the fringes of Videha kingdom, and on hearing this, the illustrious king Janaka arranged for welcome ceremonies at the outskirts of the city.
notes: These formalities are still prevalent in marriage functions, in one way or the other, in India, esp. rural India. The bridegroom's party will be received at the outskirts of the bride's place, esp. if it were to be a village, then a small function / ceremony will be held laudatory to the bridegroom, and then they are invited into that place of bride like, 'meet a party halfway...' type protocol. This is other than barāt 'matrimonial pageantry...'

glosses.meaning: at Videha kingdom, reached nearby - reached fringes of Videha

verses.devanagari:
ततो राजानमासाद्य वृद्धं दशरथं नृपम् |
जनको मुदितो राजा हर्षं च परमं ययौ
verses.iast:
tato rājānam āsādya vṛddham daśaratham nṛpam |
janako mudito rājā harṣam ca paramam yayau
verses.translation: Then the king Janaka who is by far gladdened went into a state of ecstatic elation when he met the senescent king and paladin of people, namely Dasharatha, as the pace for the marriage celebrations is quickened because of the immediate arrival of Dasharatha.

glosses.meaning: king, gladdened, Janaka nR^I pam raajaanam vR^iddham dasharatham = people's, paladin, king, senescent, towards Dasharatha
[a state of ] ecstatic, elation, went into.

verses.devanagari:
उवाच वचनं श्रेष्ठो नरश्रेष्ठं मुदान्वितम् |
स्वागतं ते नरश्रेष्ठः दिष्ट्या प्राप्तोऽसि राघव
पुत्रयोरुभयोः प्रीतिं लप्स्यसे वीर्यनिर्जिताम् |
verses.iast:
uvāca vacanam śreṣṭho naraśreṣṭham mudā anvitam |
svāgatam te naraśreṣṭhaḥ diṣṭyā prāpto asi rāghava
putrayoḥ ubhayoḥ prītim lapsyase vīrya nirjitām |
verses.translation: And the best one among men, king Janaka, gleefully said this commendable sentence to Dasharatha, the best legatee of Raghu, "oh, king, a hearty welcome to you. Oh, legatee of Ragu, your arrival to my city is just by my providence... you will now get delectation on seeing your sons who won accolades just by their valorousness in the act of raising and breaking Shiva's bow...
notes: Though Rama alone broke the bow of Shiva, both Rama and Lakshmana are said to have done it. This is a common unified laudation used for both of them, in view of their insuperable brotherhood, and such a sort of commingling both, for one person's action, can be heard often. For e.g., when Lakshmana misshapes Shuurpanakha, Rama is said to have done, and even both are said to have done that act.

glosses.meaning: to man, the best [born in foremost lineage of Raghu-s, Dasharatha, the legatee of Raghu]
providentially, bechanced [you have come,] you are

verses.devanagari:
दिष्ट्या प्राप्तो महातेजा वसिष्ठो भगवानृषिः
सह सर्वैर्द्विजश्रेष्ठैर्देवैरिव शतक्रतुः |
verses.iast:
diṣṭyā prāpto mahātejā vasiṣṭho bhagavān ṛṣiḥ
saha sarvaiḥ dvija śreṣ.hṭhaiḥ devaiḥ iva śatakratuḥ |
verses.translation: "Providentially bechanced is the arrival of this great-resplendent and godly sage Vashishta, who arrived here with all of these eminent Brahmans, like Indra himself with all gods...

glosses.meaning: with all, Brahmans, eminent ones, along with
with gods, Indra [who had to perform 'shata' hundred 'kratu' Vedic-ritual s in his earlier human birth,] as with

verses.devanagari:
दिष्ट्या मे निर्जिता विघ्ना दिष्ट्या मे पूजितं कुलम्
राघवैः सह संबंधाद्वीर्यश्रेष्ठैर्महात्मभिः |
verses.iast:
diṣṭyā me nirjitā vighnā diṣṭyā me pūjitam kulam
rāghavaiḥ saha sambandhāt vīrya śreṣṭhaiḥ mahātmabhiḥ |
verses.translation: "Providentially my hindrances are overcome by the arrival of godlike sages, and providentially my lineage too is gloried owing to this hymeneal engagement with noble-souled Raghava-s, who are the most valorous among all the valorous people...

glosses.meaning: among valorous ones, the best ones

verses.devanagari:
श्वः प्रभाते नरेन्द्र त्वम् सम्वर्तयितुमर्हसि
यज्ञस्यान्ते नरश्रेष्ठ विवाहमृषिसत्तमैः |
verses.iast:
śvaḥ prabhāte narendra tvam samvar.htayitum ar.hhasi
yajñasya ante naraśreṣṭha vivāham ṛṣi sattamaiḥ |
verses.translation: "Because you are born in first and foremost Ikshvaku dynasty, hence you are the Indra of Indra-like kings on earth... and hence, it will be apt of you to initiate the celebrations of marriage tomorrow, and the marriage itself after the culmination of the Vedic-ritual in three or four days, and the date and time for the marriage, that which is agreeable to the best sages can be decided, and you can get it performed on that date, through those great sages...
notes: There is controversy about the marriage of Seetha with Rama, insofar as its categorisation. Whether it is one of the eight kinds or not, is a debated point. The eight kinds of marriages are brāhma, daiva, prājāpatya, ārṣa, asura, gandharva, rākśasa, paiśāca and this topic can be discussed at a later time.

glosses.meaning: among men, best in first-born-linage [because you are born in first and foremost Ikshvaku dynasty, hence you are]
oh, Indra of Indra-like kings [on earth]
Vedic-ritual, at end of [at the culmination]
with Sages, best one's [conducted by, agreeable to for the time and date of marriage]
to clearly initiate [about the talks, celebrations reg. marriage,] apt of you.

verses.devanagari:
तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा ऋषिमध्ये नराधिपः
वाक्यं वाक्यविदां श्रेष्ठः प्रत्युवाच महीपतिम् |
verses.iast:
tasya tat vacanam śrutvā ṛṣi madhye narādhipaḥ
vākyam vākyavidām śreṣṭhaḥ pratyuvāca mahīpatim |
verses.translation: On hearing that sentence of king Janaka the sententious king Dasharatha replied the king Janaka from amongst the sages.

glosses.meaning: sentence, sentence, among experts, the best [sententious one - Dasharatha]

verses.devanagari:
प्रतिग्रहो दातृवशः श्रुतमेतन्मया पुरा
यथा वक्ष्यसि धर्मज्ञ तत् करिष्यामहे वयम् |
verses.iast:
pratigraho dātṛ vaśaḥ śrutam etat mayā purā
yathā vakṣyasi dharmajña tat kariṣyāmahe vayam |
verses.translation: "Recipiency rests with the restitutor... so I have heard earlier. Hence, whatever you say, for you are the knower of probity and nothing goes amiss in your astute thinking, that we will do...
notes: The word restitutor is used instead of 'donor' because Janaka is restoring the estranged divine pair to their togetherness in this mortal world. R. C. Dutt uses 'Gift betokens giver's bounty...' for this expression.

glosses.meaning: all this, earlier, by me, heard

verses.devanagari:
तद्धर्मिष्ठं यशस्यं च वचनं सत्यवादिनः
श्रुत्वा विदेहाधिपतिः परं विस्मयमागतः |
verses.iast:
tat dharmiṣṭham yaśasyam ca vacanam satya vādinaḥ
śrutvā videha adhipatiḥ param vismayam āgataḥ |
verses.translation: On listening that sentence of that affirmer of principles, namely Dasharatha, that which is conformable to the principles of marriages and familial glory, a thrill of joy came over the king of Videha. [1-69-15b. 16a]
notes: Usually the bridegroom's party will be stiff-necked at least till the marriage is over, which has become a nuisance practice in Indian marriages. Here Dasharatha is telling the opposite, by which his words are viewed as agreeable to righteousness of marriages etc., and for which Janaka is surprised.

glosses.meaning: agreeable to the principles of marriages

verses.devanagari:
ततः सर्वे मुनिगणाः परस्परसमागमे
हर्षेण महता युक्तास्तां निशामवसन् सुखम् |
verses.iast:
tataḥ sarve muni gaṇāḥ paraspara samāgame
harṣeṇa mahatā yuktāḥ tām niśām avasan sukham |
verses.translation: Then, on the forgathering of sages from Vashishta's side with the sages of Mithila all the sages have attained extreme joy and they spent that night happily.

glosses.meaning: one, to one - each other - assemblages of sages from Vashishta's side with the assemblages of sages of Mithila

verses.devanagari:
अथ रामो महातेजा लक्ष्मणेन समं ययौ
विश्वामित्रं पुरस्कृत्य पितुः पादावुपस्पृशन् |
verses.iast:
atha rāmo mahātejā lakśmaṇena samam yayau
viśvāmitram puraskṛtya pituḥ pādau upaspṛśan |
verses.translation: Then that most brilliant Rama, keeping Vishvamitra ahead, and strutting in step with Lakshmana, strutted to touch the feet of his father Dasharatha.

verses.devanagari:
राजा च राघवौ पुत्रौ निशाम्य परिहर्षितः
उवास परमप्रीतो जनकेन सुपूजितः |
verses.iast:
rājā ca rāghavau putrau niśāṃya pariharṣitaḥ
uvāsa parama prīto janakena supūjitaḥ |
verses.translation: On seeing his two sons, the super medallists in Raghu's dynasty, King Dasharatha is highly rejoiced and he resided in Mithila with a high contentment, for the reverence of Janaka is that high.
notes: The expression of 'medallists' to the word Raghava-s as above will look odd. So an explanation to this is furnished in the endnote.

glosses.meaning: sons, Raghava-s [Rama and Lakshmana, here the epithet's subtext is 'the super medallists of Raghu's dynasty]

verses.devanagari:
जनकोऽपि महातेजाः क्रियां धर्मेण तत्त्ववित् |
यज्ञस्य च सुताभ्यां च कृत्वा रात्रिमुवास ह
verses.iast:
janako api mahātejāḥ kriyā dharmeṇa tattvavit |
yajñasya ca sutābhyām ca kṛtvā rātrim uvāsa ha
verses.translation: Even the great-resplendent Janaka on performing ritual acts according to scriptures for the Vedic-ritual on hand, and the preparatory rituals for handing out both of his daughters in marriage, went into the sleep of the just, with his palm on his chest.
notes: The marriages will be commenced with initial ceremonies called ankura āropaṇa ādi kriyāḥ for an unhindered marriage function and for the harmonious family life of the newly wed.

glosses.meaning: night, resided, indeed [went into the sleep of the just with his palm on chest.]
